title: spillover-reservoir-batcher: guard against queue-starvation and KV-heavy tails
author: Asha Menon
description:
Motivation: In production traffic patterns we've observed recurring tail-latency spikes when a small proportion of KV-heavy requests starve the continuous batcher queue. The existing continuous-batcher groups by sequence length and preferences but did not have a bounded 'spillover reservoir' for requests that cannot be immediately coalesced; long-lived KV-pinned requests could occupy soft slots and cause p95/p99 regressions for small, latency-sensitive requests. This PR introduces a spillover-reservoir mechanism + deadline-aware eviction to prevent starvation and jitter for low-latency request classes.

What this changes (single contiguous description): Adds a bounded spillover reservoir per batcher shard that temporarily holds requests that missed the active coalescing window and are KV-pin heavy. Reservoir entries have two timers: a short requeue deadline (for low-latency retries) and a soft eviction deadline (for graceful fallback to a compatible, slightly cheaper model variant or to a warmed-up hot-swap lane). We also add a small fairness faucet that enforces per-class admission caps so a single tenant or request class cannot flood the batcher. The scheduler changes include: (1) admission token accounting for reservoir + active queue, (2) deadline-aware dequeue policy that prioritizes small-latency classes when their requeue timer expires, (3) adaptive lease decay on long-running KV-pinned requests to release slots gradually, and (4) a config knob `spillover_reservoir_size` and `spillover_deadline_ms` with conservative defaults.

Benchmarks: Microbench marks run on a 4xA100 testbed with mixed workload (90% short chat, 10% KV-heavy long prefix). Compared to main at commit HEAD: p50 unchanged (~22ms), p95 improved from 240ms -> 175ms (-27%), p99 improved from 520ms -> 390ms (-25%), overall token throughput impacted -1.8% under synthetic mix. Under KV-heavy spikes (burst factor 3x), the main branch saw p99 climb above 1s; this branch keeps p99 <= 420ms in the same scenario due to bounded reservoir and prioritized dequeue.

Compatibility and rollout: Defaults are conservative; feature is off for Dedicated clusters by default and on for Hosted with a rollout config gating it behind release flag `continuous_batcher_spillover_v1`. We provide runtime knobs surfaced in the Console under batcher tuning. Operator guidance: start with spillover_reservoir_size=16 and spillover_deadline_ms=50 in high-latency sensitive workloads and increase reservoir for throughput-oriented workloads.

Testing: Unit tests for the reservoir lifecycle and deadline handling added; integration bench harness included in `runtime/bench/bench_spillover.py`. Manual soak on a shadow environment (24h) validating fairness caps and no token leakage.

Risks & mitigations: If misconfigured reservoir sizes may increase transient latency for throughput-optimized queues; mitigation: conservative defaults and a circuit-breaker metric (`batcher.reservoir_pressure`) that flips the feature off automatically when sustained pressure observed.

Related: ENG-4892 (KV-heavy tail investigation), PR #20512 (queue-timeout guard) for historical context.

review_comments: Diego Ramos: Please add a metric that surfaces reservoir occupancy percent and make sure it's tagged by tenant and model_variant. We need this in the Console for rollout visibility.

release_notes: Adds a bounded spillover reservoir to the continuous batcher to reduce tail latency under KV-heavy workloads; exposes config knobs 'spillover_reservoir_size' and 'spillover_deadline_ms' and a 'batcher.reservoir_occupancy' metric. Default conservative rollout behind feature flag.
notes_testing_and_rollout: Rollout plan: feature flag rollout over 2 weeks, start with 5% of Hosted traffic, validate 'batcher.reservoir_occupancy' and 'batcher.spillover_evictions' metrics, then 25%/50%/100% steps. Dedicated customers require opt-in. Monitor p95/p99 and throughput; fallback automated if reservoir_pressure > 0.8 for >10m.
notes_for_ops: If rolling back, flip feature flag off and set spillover_reservoir_size=0 to clear in-flight reservoirs; ensure consumers are drained before full rollback.
